title: Where the Ocean's Salt Really Comes From
description: The two sources of ocean salt and how much of seawater is salt, from NOAA and USGS.
narration: Where does all the ocean's salt come from? It comes from two places: runoff from land and openings in the seafloor. Slightly acidic rainwater erodes rocks on land. That frees ions, which rivers carry to the sea. Hydrothermal fluids from vents in the seafloor add more. Sodium and chloride account for roughly 85 percent of the ocean's dissolved ions. Roughly 3.5 percent of seawater's weight is dissolved salt. In the extremely salty Dead Sea, the dense water holds you up like a mattress.
